newsitem.title: USA: US high-yld bonds lackluster, selling anticipated.
newsitem.headline: US high-yld bonds lackluster, selling anticipated.

text.p: Soggy sentiments in the high-yield bond arena lasted through the session on Friday and prices were quoted flat to down in thin trade, including bonds of WinStar Communications Inc and Ionica Plc, dealers said.

While a dearth of trading made levels and positions hard to judge, several traders noted the market was bracing for heavier secondary selling next week -- concentrated in some of the tightly priced new issues of the past month.
Street talk suggested a plethora of high-yield issues on the road, including more than $2 billion next week, prompted the anticipation of selling.
"There's going to be a lot of secondary trading because people want to free up some cash to buy new deals," one trader said. "All the tight coupons that trade 200 over."

Investment grade spreads, meanwhile, posted no significant movement amid a dormant new issue and secondary market trade, according to players there. Lack of direction from the U.S. Treasury market, which held to tight ranges despite a report of surprisingly weak producer prices for February, was blamed for the malaise.
In late trade, the benchmark 30-year bond was quoted up 5/32 to 95-31/32 to yield 6.95 percent.

Back in high-yields, WinStar unit Winstar Equipment's $200 million 12-1/2 percent guaranteed senior secured notes were quoted at 98-1/2 bid, 99-1/2 offer at mid-afternoon, off 1/2 to one point from scattered markets late on Thursday, traders said. The bonds were part of a $300 million deal priced on Thursday that was downsized from $150 million one day prior due to tepid investor demand, according to market sources.
Credit Suisse First Boston was lead manager on the deal.
The soft market also took its toll on Ionica's $200 million 15 percent senior discount notes, which dropped 1/4 point on the bid from Thursday's close to 48 on Friday.
The Ionica zeros priced at 47.688 by BT Securities Corp.

New high-yield issues on Friday included $200 million 144A senior subordinated notes due 2009 from AMC Entertainment Inc, priced as 9-1/2s to yield 9.575 percent or 287.5 basis points over the Treasury curve via Goldman, Sachs & Co.
Price talk on the issue was between 275 basis points and 300 basis points over the curve.

Elsewhere, investors extended the long-standing trend of net inflows to high-yield mutual funds in the latest week, although the rate remained below the heady pace seen earlier this year, sources said.

Cash inflows to high-yield funds that report on a weekly basis totaled $194 million in the week ended Wednesday, according to AMG Data Services, the sources said. The figure compares with inflows of $152 million for the previous week and $527 million two weeks prior.
